what_it_is: AI agent security platform: agent gateway, runtime guardrails, agent posture and red teaming.
identity_note: NeuralTrust (neuraltrust.ai). Products are TrustGate, TrustGuard, TrustLens and TrustTest.

1.reason: TrustLens inventories agents in cloud, SaaS and endpoints, and flags unregistered shadow AI.
1.evidence: TrustLens discovers every agent in your enterprise, tracks what they're configured to do
1.verify_note: Cited page loads and supports the claim. Subs re-scored with the strict tests, no change.

2.reason: TrustGate MCP and A2A gateway governs tool access. Integrations include Copilot Studio, Claude Code and Cursor.
2.evidence: TrustGate publishes one catalog and decides which of those tools the agent can reach.
2.verify_note: Cited page loads and supports the claim. Subs re-scored with the strict tests, no change.

3.reason: TrustGuard detects multi-turn attacks, blocks inline, and forwards alerts to Sentinel, Splunk and QRadar.
3.evidence: every new alert is rendered as an OCSF Detection Finding and delivered to it in near real time
3.verify_note: Cited page loads and supports the claim. Subs re-scored with the strict tests, no change.

4.reason: TrustGuard enforces input and output policy via gateway, SDK, browser extension and platforms.
4.evidence: TrustGuard inspects every interaction and stops attacks at the moment of execution
4.verify_note: Cited page loads and supports the claim. Subs re-scored with the strict tests, no change.

5.reason: Docs map controls to EU AI Act, ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF and OWASP LLM Top 10.
5.evidence: NeuralTrust supplies technical controls and evidence your compliance programme can cite against specific articles.
5.verify_note: Cited page loads and supports the claim. Subs re-scored with the strict tests, no change.

6.reason: TrustTest runs automated adversarial attacks on models, agents and HTTP APIs, and gates CI releases.
6.evidence: drop it into CI, and gate releases on the results
6.verify_note: Cited page loads and supports the claim. Subs re-scored with the strict tests, no change.

7.reason: TrustGate enforces per-agent and per-tool RBAC with Entra ID and Okta. Agents act under forwarded user identity.
7.evidence: with access scoped per user and every call on record
7.verify_note: Only 7.2 is yes. Agent sign-in forwards the user identity, so 7.1 and 7.3 stay partial and module drops to partial.

8.reason: Model Scanner flags unsafe pickle opcodes and deserialization. Dataset and AI code scanning claims are thin.
8.evidence: Secure your AI supply chain by identifying malicious code, hidden vulnerabilities, and unsafe agent behavior before deployment.
8.verify_note: Only 8.1 is yes. MCP Scanner tests a live endpoint, which is not source scanning, so module drops to partial.

notes: Gartner named NeuralTrust in the 2025 Market Guide for AI Gateways, the 2026 Market Guide for Guardian Agents, and as a 2026 EMQ pioneer for AI application security. The Model Scanner and MCP Scanner pages are live but are no longer in the main site nav. The mirror site neuraltrust.tech lists 'Model & Code Scanning' for models, code and training datasets. That is the only dataset claim found, so 8.2 is partial. No AIBOM found, so 5.1 is partial. The EU AI Act doc marks Article 50 transparency as not covered. Module 7 yes rests mainly on 7.2 per-user tool scoping, with 7.1 and 7.3 partial.
